llm_justification.summary: This prediction market tracks whether OpenAI completes a $1T+ IPO before 2027 — a corporate-action question with no directly tradable OpenAI security. The cleanest, though still weak, public-market proxy is Microsoft (large OpenAI stakeholder), with a secondary, even weaker read-through to the AI/semiconductor complex via SMH. Any informational leak that raises IPO probability would modestly support MSFT by crystallizing its stake value, but the exposure is small relative to Microsoft's size and the IPO is a slow-moving variable, so expected 12h moves are well below the 700bps tradable threshold. Both mappings are low-confidence; treat the market as a noisy sensor here.
key_assumptions: A sharp probability move reflects genuine new information about IPO timing/valuation rather than pure speculation
Microsoft retains a material economic interest in OpenAI that markets would re-rate on IPO news
No direct OpenAI-linked tradable instrument becomes available in the window
failure_modes: The proxy (MSFT) is far too large for an OpenAI IPO signal to move it ~700bps, so no tradable signal exists
IPO speculation is already widely public and priced, making any move stale
OpenAI corporate structure (nonprofit/capped-profit) could mean IPO value accrues differently than assumed, breaking the MSFT linkage
The probability move reverses as rumor fades with no official confirmation
Semiconductor reaction is dominated by macro/earnings beta, not OpenAI-specific news, yielding spurious attribution
